observations: Single photo shows a dusty, well-worn electronic keyboard with full-size keys.
A label on the control panel clearly reads 'PSR-550'.
Keyboard shows heavy surface grime, scuffed finish, and no visible power cable or stand.
No screen is lit, no indication the unit is powered on in the photo.
Watermark 'AYOOLA IFEOLUWA / POSTED ON JIJI' overlays the image, consistent with a marketplace listing screenshot.

claims.evidence: No power-on, sound, or key-press demonstration visible in photo 0.
Photo 0 clearly shows the panel label reading 'PSR-550', not PSR-650.

risks.risk: Unit may not power on or may have faulty keys/buttons despite 'working perfectly' claim.
risks.proof: A video clip of the keyboard powered on, keys being pressed, and sound playing.

risks.risk: Display screen could be dead or dim (not visible lit in photo).
risks.proof: Photo or clip showing the LCD screen illuminated with menu text.

risks.risk: Missing power adapter, stand, or pedal which affects usability and total cost.
risks.proof: Photo of included accessories (adapter, stand, pedal) laid out together.

risks.risk: Physical/internal damage from heavy visible grime and wear (possible liquid or dust ingress).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of keybed, speaker grille, and internal vents.
risks.if_unproven: priced at worst case cosmetic/functional condition

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powered on, playing a demo song or pressing multiple keys with sound.
Close-up photo of the lit LCD display.
Photo of the power adapter and any accessories included in the sale.
Wider shot showing the full keyboard and underside/serial number for condition confirmation.
response.reason: Photo confirms a Yamaha PSR-550 keyboard (contradicting the stated PSR650), but 'working perfectly' is unverified and the unit shows heavy wear with no power-on proof, so it must be priced at the worst-case non-working condition against comparable basic Yamaha PSR-series keyboards.
